findings.title: float:right on .small-action button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container
findings.body: The PR adds `@include flexbox()` and `@include align-items(center)` to `.small-action`, which makes all of its direct children flex items. Per the flexbox spec, `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule (lines 306-310) silently stops working: a button rendered inside a small-action post that was previously pinned to the right edge will now sit inline immediately after `.small-action-desc`. To preserve the old right-aligned behavior the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or `justify-content`/`order` adjustments) instead of `float: right`. The same applies to the leftover `clear: both` on line 312 and the `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` (line 270), which are now dead declarations under the flex layout.

findings.title: Panel right alignment relies on margin-left:auto, which breaks in browsers that only support the legacy -webkit-box flex syntax
findings.body: `.panel` previously used `float: right` to sit at the right edge of the header; it now relies on `margin-left: auto` plus `@include order(3)` inside the new flex container. The `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -webkit-box` / `display: -moz-box` for legacy engines, but the 2009 flexbox spec does not honor auto margins for alignment (it used `box-pack`), and `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`order` behavior also differs. On any client that falls back to the legacy box display, the panel will no longer be pushed to the right. If supporting those engines is the reason the legacy prefixes were added, the panel needs a fallback (e.g. keep a float fallback or use box-pack: justify).
